chunks: And what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man and a woman who both perish, and the heirs of the woman come and claim the dowry against the heirs of the man. He said, 'And they have perished and the inheritance has been distributed?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'They have nothing.' I said, 'And if the woman is alive and comes after the death of her husband claiming her dowry?' He said, 'She has nothing, for she remained with him acknowledging [the debt] until her husband perished.' I said, 'And if she dies while he is alive, and her heirs come to claim her dowry from him?' He said, 'She remained until she died, not claiming it.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'She has nothing.' I said, 'And if he divorces her and she comes claiming her dowry, having remained not claiming it until he divorced her?' He said, 'She has nothing.' I said, 'When is the limit, that if she claims it, she has nothing?' He said, 'When she is presented to him and enters his house, and claims after that, she has nothing. It is much for her that an oath be taken by Allah that she has no dowry from him; little, not much.'

key_terms.أُهْدِيَتْ إِلَيْهِ: Presented to him (in the context of marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on claiming dowry if both spouses die simultaneously or if the wife remains silent about it after entering the husband's house?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential principle that the wife's right to the full dowry (mahr) is contingent upon her claim before consummation or cohabitation; once she enters the husband's house, the debt is considered effectively settled or limited to a sworn oath of non-payment. Al-Tusi uses this narration to distinguish between the legal status of the dowry as a debt versus a right that is extinguished by the act of dwelling together, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding marital financial obligations. The ruling emphasizes that silence or delay in claiming the dowry during cohabitation implies acceptance of the marital bond's fulfillment, thereby barring subsequent claims by heirs or the wife herself after divorce or death.
